question.text: Mr. Patel invested in a balanced advantage fund. Six months later, the AMC changes the scheme's investment objective from "dynamic equity-debt allocation" to "pure equity growth." What is Mr. Patel's right in this situation?

answer.text: He must receive a written notice and can exit at the prevailing NAV without any exit load
He has no special rights since the AMC can change investment objectives at any time
He can demand the AMC buy back his units at the original purchase NAV
He must wait for the change to be approved by SEBI before he can exit

explanation.text: The Logic: A change in investment objective is a change in fundamental attributes. The AMC must send a written communication to all unitholders like Mr. Patel, publish an advertisement, and provide a 30-day exit option at the prevailing NAV without any exit load. In addition, the trustees shall take the comments of the Board (SEBI) before bringing such change. This package protects investors who invested based on the original scheme character. The Trap: The AMC cannot change fundamental attributes without giving unitholders the load-free exit option, so investors do have specific rights. The exit is at prevailing NAV, not the original purchase NAV. Note: Lock in the source-supported package: written communication, advertisement, 30-day exit at prevailing NAV without exit load, and trustees taking Board comments before implementing the change.
